thread.title: Unity Rules Engine Development
thread.preview:
**I recommend presenting the three movement proposals together as NEW provisional policy.** They are coherent with the sourced movement/Press sequence for the fixed-roster, five-foot-step host. Tighten the following boundaries before presenting them; none is adopted by this review.

**NEW movement completion — recommended wording**

1. **Ordinary OA window.** Capture all initially eligible ordinary OA reactors in the existing encounter initiative order. Revalidate before each offer and before committing an accepted response. Each controller chooses for its own creature. The captured list does not gain newly eligible reactors during that window—make this explicit as part of the new snapshot policy.

   After the first offer, the mover cannot voluntarily cancel, change destination or substitute another movement mode. State changes may invalidate the announced step. If that happens, discard outstanding offers **without spending those creatures’ unused Reactions**. Already resolved attacks, spent Reactions, dice and consequences remain committed.

   After the responses, revalidate the fixed step against current permissions, occupancy, Speed and movement allowance. Debit movement only when the step completes. A step with no eligible offers completes directly after validation.

2. **Press retreat predicate.** For the supported geometry, Press requires the target’s completed voluntary step to change it from adjacent to **not adjacent** to the Press holder. Remaining adjacent after lateral movement does not qualify.

   Evaluate the actual before/after movement event after pre-exit reactions. An announced step that never occurs creates no vacated-space trigger. This is a **new precise definition of “retreat,”** not wording recovered from the source.

3. **Press commitment.** Revalidate the follow’s destination, body permissions and separate five-foot movement-cost allowance before accepting it. Acceptance immediately consumes that regular-turn interval’s follow entitlement. Its own pre-exit OAs can prevent travel without refunding that entitlement.

   If travel never occurs, credit no physical distance, spend no distance-based movement cost and consume no Mobile distance. The accepted Press entitlement remains spent. A completed follow uses **Press’s separate budget**, never the ordinary movement ledger. Declining the follow does not consume it.

These additions preserve the sourced distinctions between pre-exit OA, actual movement and subsequent Press. They also prevent an interrupted movement command from rolling back the attack that stopped it. [Combat §§Maneuvers and ordinary attacks; Movement and geometry](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/4ba6b4ca095dc2f78323ca26198570812eaeef56/DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/mechanics/COMBAT_ACTION_PLAYTEST.md#maneuvers-and-ordinary-attacks).

Two scope limits should accompany the package:

- Initiative priority applies to **ordinary OA offers**, not globally to Ready, Interpose or other effect windows. Preserve existing application ordering for competing recorded Press effects.
- Every potentially eligible reactor must be represented. “Not in this encounter roster” cannot silently suppress a nearby creature’s otherwise legal OA. Such a situation remains outside the fixed-roster host until its entry policy is supported.

**The ordinary unarmed profile is only partly explicit**

| Component | What the inspected sources establish |
|---|---|
| Base damage | **Flat 1 bludgeoning**, not `1d1` or a rolled damage die. V6 equipment table, line 6776. |
| Attack classification and reach | Unarmed strikes are melee attacks; ordinary reach is usually 5 ft. This establishes ordinary OA eligibility. |
| Attack ability | STR for melee unless an actual exception applies. STR10 therefore contributes **+0**. |
| Attack proficiency | No universal unarmed-proficiency grant was located. Require an actual covering grant. Your numerical actors have none; **add no PB**. |
| Damage ability modifier | V6 explicitly adds the attack ability modifier to **weapon attacks**. Applying that to ordinary unarmed requires resolving the weapon-attack classification discussed below. STR10 makes the numerical contribution zero either way. |
| Critical treatment | Double damage **dice**, not flat damage or modifiers. The ordinary flat 1 remains 1; there is no damage die to roll or double. Preserve the critical flag for other consequences, including damage at zero HP. |
| Body/hand requirement | Unarmed strike is an attack option, not an inventory object. The inspected general clauses do not give a complete usable-body-part rule or explicitly require a free hand. |

Primary pointers: [V6 unarmed table entry](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/4ba6b4ca095dc2f78323ca26198570812eaeef56/docs/reference/Player_Rulebook_v6_source_text.txt#L6762), [attack ability and proficiency](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/4ba6b4ca095dc2f78323ca26198570812eaeef56/docs/reference/Player_Rulebook_v6_source_text.txt#L8177), [damage and critical rules](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/4ba6b4ca095dc2f78323ca26198570812eaeef56/docs/reference/Player_Rulebook_v6_source_text.txt#L8229), [Equipment §Record possessions and permissions](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/4ba6b4ca095dc2f78323ca26198570812eaeef56/DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/mechanics/EQUIPMENT_ACQUISITION_PLAYTEST.md#record-possessions-and-permissions).

There is useful additional provenance for proficiency: **FS-02’s FAA-03 amendment** retains ordinary Unarmed strike as a Simple-melee **training entry**, with actual Simple-weapons or express unarmed training supplying proficiency. But its profile-classification bridge explicitly says **“limited to Weapon Focus and Weapon Mastery.”** It does not supply everyone proficiency or settle every weapon-attack rider. Warrior’s first-class list remains Martial weapons only. [FS-02, `/rules/1/wording`](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/4ba6b4ca095dc2f78323ca26198570812eaeef56/DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/data/public/feat_candidates/exact_01/shared_rules.json), [character foundation](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/4ba6b4ca095dc2f78323ca26198570812eaeef56/DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/mechanics/CHARACTER_FOUNDATION_TABLES.md#first-class-armor-weapons-and-tools).

**Aggressive and anatomy still need an explicit completion**

The table’s Simple Melee Weapons placement supports a weapon-attack interpretation. However, the general combat clause explicitly establishes only **melee attack**, and the later training bridge is scoped. I would not silently turn that into a settled ruling that Aggressive applies.

I recommend a **separate NEW ordinary-unarmed completion** for the owner:

> Ordinary unarmed strikes use STR for attack and damage. Before defenses, damage is `max(0, 1 + STR modifier + applicable flat damage modifiers)`, bludgeoning. They count as melee weapon attacks for Aggressive and the ordinary ability-to-damage rule, while remaining attack options rather than held inventory weapons. This grants no proficiency, equipment properties or class features.

For anatomy, propose explicitly:

> A supported ordinary humanoid may deliver the strike with an actually usable fist, elbow, knee, foot or head. A free hand is not required when another permitted striking body part is usable. Actual conditions and specific body restrictions still apply; this grants no anatomy, extra reach or permission for arbitrary transformed bodies.

That anatomy paragraph is **new policy**, not recovered text. Until decided, your current fixture can supply an explicitly usable free fist as a **fixture fact**, without claiming a universal hand requirement.

With that additional unarmed completion adopted, the STR10/no-proficiency actors would have:

| Situation | Attack modifier before other effects | Damage before defenses |
|---|---:|---:|
| Ordinary unarmed hit or critical | +0 | 1 bludgeoning |
| Aggressive unarmed hit or critical | +0 | 3 bludgeoning |

Without that adoption, base damage, STR attack ability, absent PB and flat critical treatment are supported; **Aggressive applicability and the general body-use contract remain unresolved**.

content.text:
I agree with your movement sequencing and the recommendation to do Stand/DropProne plus ordinary unarmed/Reaction continuations before departure movement. Condition projections now pass591 tests; this also separates capacity-only Exhaustion recomputation from actual lethal track changes per MAXIMUM_HP_PLAYTEST. No arbitrary conditions have been admitted into schema9 yet.

I checked the local Combat movement/Press source and found the same three unresolved areas. Please review these NEW provisional completion proposals so we can present one concrete set to the owner (none adopted yet): (1) For an announced single step, capture eligible ordinary OA reactors in existing encounter initiative order, ask each controller in that order, revalidate before each offer, and discard unspent offers if an earlier response makes that departure impossible. No voluntary cancellation after the first reaction offer; only state-caused invalidation can stop that committed step. Movement expenditure occurs only when the step actually completes. (2) A Press trigger requires voluntary movement from adjacent to no longer adjacent; moving laterally while remaining adjacent is not retreat for Press. (3) Accepting an eligible Press follow consumes that turn's one follow immediately; an intervening OA can stop travel without refunding the entitlement, and no movement distance is credited if travel never occurs. Does this combination create any contradiction with sourced action/movement/Press rules, or does it need a different concrete completion? Explicitly label all new policy.

Also confirm the complete ordinary unarmed attack profile for the numerical STR10 actors: exact base damage, ability modifier, attack proficiency (if source explicitly grants it), whether Aggressive weapon-attack damage applies, critical flat damage treatment, and usable-body/hand requirement. V6 lines8195-8199 prove melee classification and OA eligibility but do not themselves supply all those details. Avoid importing D&D defaults where our actual text is silent.
